bundle_cancer_screening/dist/medicaid_ca.long_name: Medicaid and CHIP Cancer Screening Rate
bundle_cancer_screening/dist/medicaid_ca.short_description: Percentage of Medicaid and CHIP beneficiaries who received cancer screening.
bundle_cancer_screening/dist/medicaid_ca.long_description: State-level cancer screening rates for Medicaid and CHIP beneficiaries, from the Medicaid and CHIP Adult Core Set Quality Measures voluntarily reported by states to CMS (2014–2023). Includes breast cancer screening (BCS: women aged 50–74 who received a mammogram), cervical cancer screening (CCS: women aged 21–64 who received appropriate cervical cancer screening), and colorectal cancer screening (COL: adults aged 50–75 who received appropriate colorectal cancer screening). Reporting is voluntary; not all states report all measures each year.

bundle_cancer_screening/dist/cms_cancer_.short_description: Percentage of Medicare FFS beneficiaries who received cancer screening, by state and age group.
bundle_cancer_screening/dist/cms_cancer_.long_description: State-level cancer screening utilization rates for Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries from the CMS Mapping Medicare Disparities (MMD) by Population Tool. Includes mammogram (breast cancer screening), pap test (cervical cancer screening), colorectal cancer screening, and prostate cancer screening. Rates reflect the percentage of Medicare FFS beneficiaries who utilized each preventive screening service. Stratified by age group.

Age group at diagnosis in years. Groups overlap: '<1', '1-4', '5-9', '10-14', '15-19', '20-24', '25-29', '30-39' are disjoint; '0-19', '15-39', '20-39', and '0-39' are aggregates.

bundle_cancer_screening/dist/nccr_incide.long_name: Age-Adjusted Childhood, Adolescent and Young Adult Cancer Incidence Rate by ICCC Site
bundle_cancer_screening/dist/nccr_incide.short_description: Age-adjusted annual incidence rate per 1,000,000 of the ICCC cancer site named in `outcome_name`, among ages 0-39, national level.
bundle_cancer_screening/dist/nccr_incide.long_description: Age-adjusted annual incidence rate per 1,000,000 population for the ICCC diagnostic group in `outcome_name`, among children, adolescents, and young adults (ages 0-39), from the National Childhood Cancer Registry (NCCR*Explorer). Rates are pooled across ~29 U.S. cancer registries covering ~76% of the U.S. population and are age-adjusted to the 2000 U.S. standard population. Stratified by sex, race/ethnicity, and age group. A value of 0 is only meaningful when both `suppressed_flag` and `not_collected_flag` are 0; suppressed or not-collected cells were set to 0 in the source.

bundle_cancer_screening/dist/nccr_incide.long_name: Suppression flag for the rate in this row
bundle_cancer_screening/dist/nccr_incide.short_description: Binary indicator: 1 if NCCR*Explorer suppressed the rate for this cell (fewer than 16 cases), in which case `value` is 0; 0 otherwise.

bundle_cancer_screening/dist/nccr_incide.long_name: Not-collected flag for the rate in this row
bundle_cancer_screening/dist/nccr_incide.short_description: Binary indicator: 1 if the statistic was not collected/not available for this cell, in which case `value` is 0; 0 otherwise.

nccr.name: National Childhood Cancer Registry Explorer (NCCR*Explorer)
nccr.organization: National Cancer Institute (NCI), Childhood Cancer Data Initiative
nccr.location: NCCR*Explorer: An interactive website for NCCR cancer statistics
nccr.description: The National Childhood Cancer Registry (NCCR) is a federated data resource maintained by the National Cancer Institute (NCI) as part of the Childhood Cancer Data Initiative (CCDI). NCCR*Explorer provides precalculated incidence statistics for cancers among children, adolescents, and young adults (ages 0-39) diagnosed from 2001 forward, pooled from up to 29 U.S. cancer registries representing approximately 76% of the U.S. population ages 0-39. Cancers are classified using the International Classification of Childhood Cancer (ICCC). Rates are age-adjusted to the 2000 U.S. standard population and reported at the national level only.
nccr.restrictions: Public domain. Data from the National Childhood Cancer Registry, produced by the National Cancer Institute, is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.
